title: Suzuki Roshi, Something Else, Zen Practice is Useless
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett takes up the posture chapter of Suzuki Roshi's Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind, after announcements about ill sangha members and the $550,000 capital campaign for a building. Nomon recalls Zoketsu Norman Fischer saying Zen practice is useless, reads Holly Hughes's poem about the mind wanting more, and works through three points: the posture as a practice of "not two and not one," zazen as a chance to allow something to happen, and the close link between body and mind. Nomon also tells of visiting Jakusho Kwong Roshi on Sonoma Mountain, where an expansion permit triggered over a million dollars in code upgrades. Nomon closes by assigning homework: reread Suzuki Roshi's posture directions on page twenty-six.
